title: Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards Cardholder Terms — Holding Several Cards
content:
**Clause.** A customer may hold any number of Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards: no maximum number of cards per customer is set. Each card number keeps its own balance, its own expiry and its own rules. A balance moves between cards only by a transfer — either a consolidation of one card's balance onto another card, or the move of a lost or stolen card's balance to a replacement card.

## The clause in parts

| Matter | Position |
|---|---|
| Number of cards one customer may hold | Any number; no maximum is set |
| Balance | Kept separately on each card number |
| Expiry | Kept separately on each card number |
| Rules of the card kind | Kept separately on each card number |
| How value passes from one card to another | Only by a transfer: a consolidation, or a lost or stolen card's balance moved to a replacement |

The balance of a card number is the value available on it. Issues, reloads, refunds and transfers in raise it; redemptions, transfers out, cash-outs, expiry and bonus forfeiture lower it.

## Questions the clause answers

**Does holding a second card change anything on the first?** No. Each card number keeps its own balance, expiry and rules, whatever other cards the same customer holds.

**Are the balances of two cards held by one customer pooled into one figure?** No. They remain two balances on two card numbers; value passes between them only by a transfer of one of the two kinds named in the clause.

### Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical customer holds a Marlowe & Finch Gift Card with $35.00, a Merchandise Credit Card with $60.00 and a Registry Reward Card with $80.00. The customer holds three balances, not one balance of $175.00; the Registry Reward Card keeps its own expiry, and the two cards that do not expire do not take it on.
